title: Addressing Challenges in India’s Public Health Landscape: District-Level Deprivations in Public Health Infrastructure and Services
content: Background: Primary Health Care (PHC) is widely recognized as the cornerstone of equitable progress towards Universal Health Coverage (UHC). In India’s decentralized health governance, district-level disparities in PHC capacity are often obscured by state-level aggregates. Objective: This study introduces a district-level PHC Inputs Index (PHCII), applying it to two contrasting states – Jharkhand and Karnataka – to capture subnational variation and examine its association with UHC outcomes. Methods: Using the Primary Health Care Performance Initiative (PHCPI) framework, the index integrates 14 indicators across six domains: performance, quality, capacity, access, financing, and governance. Data from the Health Management Information System (HMIS), Rural Health Statistics (RHS), and the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) were analyzed for 24 districts in Jharkhand and 30 in Karnataka, with composite scores computed across two time periods. Spatial and statistical methods, including binary classification, tercile grouping, and GIS mapping, were employed to assess trends and relationships. Results: Our findings reveal substantial intra-state heterogeneity. Jharkhand showed incremental improvements in select districts, while Karnataka exhibited stronger baseline capacity but declines in financing and governance. A generally positive association between PHC inputs and UHC outcomes was observed, although misalignments highlight persistent demand-side barriers and adaptive service delivery mechanisms. Conclusion: The PHC Index demonstrates policy utility as a replicable tool for district-level planning, enabling data-informed strategies to strengthen equity and advance UHC in India.
